name: Puerto Rico
blurb: Colonial forts, rainforest hikes and glowing bays, with no passport needed for US citizens.
cities: San Juan
Colourful Old San Juan, Spanish forts and salsa nights.
El Yunque
Rainforest trails and waterfalls in a US national forest.
Vieques
Bioluminescent bay kayaking and wild horses on quiet beaches.
Culebra
Flamenco Beach and snorkelling with turtles.
Ponce
The 'Pearl of the South', with a striped firehouse and an art museum.
Aguadilla & Rincón
World-class surf and sunsets on the northwest coast.
Mayagüez
A west-coast university city, with boats to Mona Island.
Arecibo
Río Camuy's karst caves and a historic radio observatory site.
Guayama
A quiet southern coast town with colonial architecture.
Fajardo & Luquillo
Laguna Grande's glowing bio bay, catamaran trips to Icacos and Luquillo Beach's food kiosks.
Cabo Rojo
Los Morrillos lighthouse on limestone cliffs, Playa Sucia and pink salt flats.
La Parguera & Guánica
A bioluminescent bay, mangrove cays and the cactus-dotted Guánica Dry Forest.
Camuy River Cave Park
A giant sinkhole and cavern system carved by one of the world's largest underground rivers.
Central Mountains (Jayuya & Toro Negro)
Coffee farms, Taíno petroglyphs and cloud forest trails along the Ruta Panorámica.
San Germán
The island's second-oldest town, with the 17th-century Porta Coeli church.
Isabela
Surf breaks, Jobos Bay and clifftop trails on the northwest coast.
Dorado
Beach resorts, golf and calm swimming coves 30 minutes west of San Juan.
Mona Island
A remote nature reserve of sea cliffs, caves and rock iguanas, visited by permit.
